newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 12.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Constitution Scrutiny Committee has come under intense military pressure to delete clauses in the draft to deny amnesty to coup plotters and give people the right to resist an armed seizure of power. The objections cause some members of the committee to seek to bow to the demands, claiming the denial of amnesty to those who prepare, attempt or stage a coup may lead to violence. (BANGKOK POST)

- Interior Minister Snoh Thienthong has confirmed that his New Aspiration Party (NAP) is wooing Thaksin Shinawatra to join the NAP, while a source close to the telecom billionaire says his wish to return to politics has been mixed with fears of the prime minister's "cunning". Speculation about Thaksin's future is further fuelled on the eve of a crucial government meeting that will bring together rival economic teams - the Chart Pattana Party and non-MP cabinet members led by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan. (THE NATION)

- Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobamrung, chairman of the controversial media-monitoring committee, has just stumbled on one of the challenges of his new job - convincing foreign journalists that his role is relevant. While Chalerm is still arguing with the foreign press, his boss, Interior Minister Snoh Thienthong, may have compounded the problem by announcing that from now on the government and the press must jointly manage the news. (THE NATION)

- The Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) has finally agreed to reveal all information about the Yadana gas pipeline project, including details of the contract it signed with the Burmese government. Pala Sookawesh, PTT's governor, says that his agency will reveal contract details to the provincial sub-committee in Kanchanaburi today. (THE NATION)

- State-owned Telephone Organisation of Thailand (TOT)'s board of directors has surprised many by agreeing to form a joint venture with Jasmine International Plc to operate its cellular NMT470 MHz system. Earlier, the TOT called for a closed-bid to find a service provider for its cellular system, but later decided to allow the private firm to develop and operate in its cellular market. (THE NATION)
